catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.home.v1 publishes an optional numeric speed_scale input, but the native home command homes every configured device and takes no speed; a class binding would have to refuse or ignore that input, and G3 requires a limit for it. The extension has an empty input and reports which axes were homed.
catalogue_requests.summary: Home all three axes with the native home command (command 1).

catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.stop.v1 publishes an optional numeric deceleration input, but the native emergency stop is a broadcast of command 23 with no deceleration parameter. The extension has an empty input, calls that native stop, and is the safe-state action SAFE-045 requires for this model-written R2 package.
catalogue_requests.summary: Stop every axis with the native emergency-stop broadcast; the safe state.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend only: python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/hgomersall__pyzaber --backend fake exited 0 with G1-G6, G8 and G9 pass and G7 warn (four MAYBE_ABSENT warnings). Evidence is contract_checked; no MHS-Device level is claimed. No hardware was attached, no hardware backend exists, and the upstream clone was never imported, installed or run. The package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the required model entry and reviewed_by is null; no human reviewed or tested anything here.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card proposes a SerialDriver (family serial, decision family-config), but the clone is not a text protocol: serial_connection.send_command writes a (device_id, command, data) frame that async_serial packs with struct (pyzaber/serial_connection.py:144-150, 507-510), and the commands are numbers in the clone's tables (pyzaber/zaber_device.py:10-29). The package is therefore a direct Driver over the card entry symbol pyzaber.linear_slides:multiaxis_linear_slides; no wire syntax was changed and no command table was invented.

Coverage: reads x_mm, y_mm and z_mm in millimetres from get_current_position; cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 performs an absolute X/Y/Z move through the upstream blocking move_absolute and reads the positions back; x-cap.hgomersall.home_axes.v1 sends the native home command; x-cap.hgomersall.stop_motion.v1 and the @estop method call native emergency_stop, which broadcasts command 23 to device 0. device_kind is robot.arm because cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 binds only robot.arm and the clone's example calls the three-axis x/y/z configuration a gantry system. risk is R2, above the card's R1 floor, because the device moves a three-axis gantry. The clone documents no independent hardware e-stop, so estop_physical_ref is not claimed; the safe-state extension is the independent stop SAFE-045 accepts, and safety.not_certified is true.

Limits: no text file of the clone states axis travel, end stops or a workspace, so position.x, position.y and position.z are Limit.operator_required. Until an operator overlay supplies them every move is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET; site-limits.example.json is an example only (0-300 mm x and y, 0-200 mm z) and is not a fact about a stage. No bound was copied from a constructor default (steps_per_rev=200 and mm_per_rev=6.35 are mechanical configuration, not device limits).

No hardware backend: the upstream modules are Python 2 (pyzaber/zaber_device.py:3 imports Queue; pyzaber/zaber_multidevice.py:64 is a Python 2 print statement) and cannot be imported by the Python 3 runtime, so no native.py is shipped and driver.lock.json backends is only {"fake": ".fake:FakePyzaber"}. This R2 package therefore has no path to hardware in this environment; any future hardware port needs a human review (reviewed_by stays null). The acceptance gate's hardware view was served over the fake object, never over the upstream code.

G7 warnings: four MAYBE_ABSENT warnings name emergency_stop, get_current_position, home and move_absolute. They are expected and cannot be cleared without changing the card's entry symbol: the upstream class declares only __init__ in its own AST and inherits the commands through from zaber_multidevice import * and the dynamic __getattr__ (pyzaber/zaber_device.py:163-196), so the gate cannot follow the external base; every name occurs in the clone.

NOT COVERED: the hardware path, the upstream Python 2 modules, the real binary serial transport and its threading, actual homing and limit-switch behaviour, set_position (it exists only in the clone's dummy simulator, not in the native class), move_relative, the clone's meta commands, the device settings reads and writes, and any MHS-Device-level evidence. The fake is an in-memory stand-in, not a recording; every number in fake.py is marked # placeholder and is test data. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; the digest above is the one the passing run printed.
